contenido: 1. The Second Vatican Council prescribed the drafting of a "Directory on the catechetical formation of the Christian people."( [+[0]+] ) In compliance with this conciliar mandate, the Congregation for the Clergy used a special Commission of experts and consulted the Episcopal Conferences of the world, which sent numerous suggestions and observations on the matter. The prepared text was reviewed by an ad hoc Theological Commission and by the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith. On March 18, 1971, it was definitively approved by Paul VI and promulgated on April 11 of the same year, with the title Directorium Catechisticum Generale.

2. The thirty years that have elapsed since the closing of the Second Vatican Council until the threshold of the third millennium constitute - without a doubt - a very rich time in guidelines and promotion of catechesis. It has been a time that, in some way, has once again made present the evangelizing vitality of the early Church and timely promoted the teachings of the Fathers, favoring the updated return to the ancient Catechumenate. Since 1971, the Directorium Catechisticum Generale has guided particular Churches on the long path of renewal of catechesis, proposing itself as a point of reference both in terms of content and in terms of pedagogy and methods to be used.

3. The Magisterium of the Church has never ceased, in these years, to perseverely exercise its pastoral care in favor of catechesis. Numerous Bishops and Episcopal Conferences, on all continents, have notably promoted catechesis, publishing valuable Catechisms and pastoral guidelines, promoting the training of experts and favoring catechetical research. These efforts have been fruitful and have had a favorable impact on the catechetical activity of the particular Churches. A particularly rich contribution to catechetical renewal was the Ritual of Christian Initiation of Adults, promulgated on January 6, 1972 by the Congregation for Divine Worship.

4. A decisive milestone for catechesis was the reflection carried out by the General Assembly of the Synod of Bishops on the evangelization of the contemporary world, which was held in October 1974. The propositions of this Assembly were presented to Pope Paul VI, who promulgated the Apostolic Exhortation Evangelii Nuntiandi, of December 8, 1975. This document presents, among others, a principle of particular importance: catechesis as action evangelizing within the scope of the general mission of the Church. Catechetical activity, from now on, must be considered as always participating in the urgencies and concerns of the missionary mandate for our time.

5. John Paul II assumed this heritage in 1978 and formulated his first guidelines in the Apostolic Exhortation Catechesi Tradendae, of October 16, 1979. This Exhortation forms a completely coherent unit with the Exhortation Evangelii Nuntiandi and fully places catechesis again in the framework of evangelization.

6. On the other hand, the General Assemblies, ordinary and extraordinary, of the Synod of Bishops have had a particular impact in the field of catechesis. Due to their particular importance, the Synodal Assemblies of 1980 and 1987, on the mission of the family and on the vocation of baptized lay people, should be noted. The synodal works were followed by the corresponding Apostolic Exhortations of John Paul II Familiaris Consortio ( [+[0]+] ) and Christifideles Laici ( [+[1]+] ). The same Extraordinary Synod of 1985 has also had a decisive influence on the present and future of catechesis in our time. On that occasion, the twenty years of application of the Second Vatican Council were reviewed, and the Synod Fathers proposed to the Holy Father the elaboration of a universal Catechism for the Catholic Church. The proposal of the Extraordinary Synod Assembly of 1985 was welcomed favorably and made his own by John Paul II. Once the patient and complex process of its preparation was completed, the Catechism of the Catholic Church was delivered to the bishops and particular Churches through the Apostolic Constitution Fidei Depositum on October 11, 1992.

7. This event of such profound significance and the set of facts and magisterial interventions previously mentioned, imposed the duty of a review of the Directorium Catechisticum Generale, in order to adapt this valuable theological-pastoral instrument to the new situation and new needs. Collecting such heritage and synthetically systematizing it in order to catechetical activity, always in the perspective of the present stage of the life of the Church, is a service of the Apostolic See to all.
8. The General Directory for Catechesis, preserving the basic structure of the 1971 text, is articulated as follows:

9. The purpose of this Directory is, obviously, the same as that pursued by the 1971 text. It is proposed, in effect, to indicate "the theological-pastoral principles of a fundamental nature—taken from the Magisterium of the Church and particularly from the Second Vatican Ecumenical Council—by which the pastoral action of the ministry of the word" and, specifically, of catechesis can be more adequately oriented and governed.( [+[0]+] ) The purpose It was and is fundamental to offer reflections and principles, rather than immediate applications or practical guidelines. Such a path and method is used, above all, for the following reason: only if from the beginning the nature and purposes of catechesis are correctly understood, as well as the truths and values that must be transmitted, can defects and errors in catechetical matters be avoided.( [+[1]+] )

10. It is evident that not all parts of the Board have the same importance. What is said about divine revelation, the nature of catechesis and the criteria with which the Christian message must be presented, has value for everyone. On the other hand, the parts that refer to the present situation, the methodology and the way of adapting catechesis to different situations of age or cultural context, should rather be received as suggestions and indications.( [+[0]+] )

11. The recipients of the Directory are mainly the Bishops, the Episcopal Conferences and, in general, those who, under their mandate and presidency, carry out a responsibility in the field of catechesis. It is obvious that the Directory can be a valid instrument for the formation of candidates for the priesthood, for the ongoing formation of priests and for the formation of catechists.

12. Since the Directory is addressed to particular Churches, whose pastoral situations and needs are very diverse, it is evident that only common or intermediate situations have been able to be taken into consideration. This also happens when the organization of catechesis at the various levels is described. When using the Directory, keep this observation in mind. As was already noted in the 1971 text, what will be insufficient in those regions where catechesis has been able to reach a high level of quality and resources, will perhaps seem excessive in those places where catechesis has not yet been able to experience such progress.

13. By publishing this document, new testimony of the concern of the Apostolic See for the catechetical ministry, it is expected that it will be received, examined and studied with great attention, taking into account the pastoral needs of each particular Church; and also that it can stimulate more in-depth studies and research in the future, which respond to the needs of catechesis and the norms and guidelines of the Magisterium of the Church.

14. This Introductory Exposition aims to stimulate pastors and catechesis agents to become aware of the need to always look at the sowing field and to do so from faith and mercy. The interpretation of the contemporary world presented here obviously has a provisional character, inherent with historical contingency.

15. This parable is an inspiring source for evangelization. « The seed is the Word of God » ( [+[0]+] ). The sower is Jesus Christ. He announced the Gospel in Palestine two thousand years ago and sent his disciples to sow it in the world. Jesus Christ, today, present in the Church through his Spirit, continues to sow the Word of the Father in the field of the world.

16. The Church continues to sow the Gospel of Jesus in God's great field. Christians, inserted in the most varied social contexts, look at the world with the same eyes with which Jesus contemplated the society of his time. The disciple of Jesus Christ, in fact, participates from within "the joys and hopes, the sadness and anguish of the men of our time", ([+[0]+] ) looks at human history and participates in it, not only with reason but with faith. In the light of this, the world appears, at the same time, "founded and preserved by the love of the Creator, enslaved under the bondage of sin and freed by Christ, crucified and resurrected, once the power of the Evil One was broken." ([+[1]+] )

17. As the mother of men, the first thing the Church sees, with profound pain, is "a huge multitude of men and women: children, adults and the elderly, in a word, of concrete and unrepeatable human persons, who suffer the intolerable weight of misery."( [+[0]+] ) She, through a catechesis in which the social teaching of the Church takes its place, ( [+[1]+] heart of Christians "the commitment to justice"([+[2]+]) and the "option or preferential love for the poor",([+[3]+]) so that their presence is truly light that illuminates and salt that transforms.

18. The Church, when analyzing the field of the world, is very sensitive to everything that affects the dignity of the human person. She knows that human rights spring from that dignity,( [+[0]+] ) the constant object of concern and commitment of Christians. That is why his gaze is not only interested in economic and social indicators,( [+[1]+] ) but also in cultural and religious ones. What it seeks is the integral development of people and towns.( [+[2]+] )

19. However, in many places, and in apparent contradiction with the sensitivity for the dignity of the person, human rights are clearly violated.( [+[0]+] ) And thus other forms of poverty are generated in those places, which are not only situated on the material level: it is a cultural and religious poverty that also concerns the ecclesial community. The denial or limitation of human rights, in effect, impoverishes the person and the people as much or more than the deprivation of material goods.( [+[1]+] )

20. The sower knows that the seed penetrates specific soil and that it needs to absorb all the necessary elements to be able to bear fruit. ( [+[0]+] ) He also knows that, sometimes, some of these elements can harm germination and the harvest.

21. Along with this "more universal form of culture",([+[0]+]) today there is also a growing desire to revalue native cultures. The Council's question remains alive: "How should the dynamism and expansion of the new culture be encouraged without perishing the living fidelity to the heritage of traditions?" ".( [+[1]+] )

22. Among the elements that make up the cultural heritage of a people, the religious-moral factor has particular relevance for the planter. In today's culture there is a persistent spread of religious indifference: "There are many who, today, ignore this intimate and vital union with God or explicitly deny it." ([+[0]+] )

23. The moral situation observed today is closely related to the religious one. In effect, an obscuration of the ontological truth of the human person is detected. And this happens as if the rejection of God wanted to mean the inner rupture of the aspirations of the human being.( [+[0]+] ) We thus witness, in many places, an "ethical relativism that removes from civil coexistence any secure point of moral reference."( [+[1]+] )

24. The disciples of Jesus are immersed in the world like leaven but, as at all times, they are not immune from experiencing the influence of human situations. Therefore, it is necessary to consider the current situation of the faith of Christians.

25. However, given the current religious panorama, it is necessary for the children of the Church to verify: «To what extent are they also affected by the atmosphere of secularism and ethical relativism? ".( [+[0]+] )

26. There is also no shortage of a certain number of baptized people who, unfortunately, hide their Christian identity either because of a poorly understood form of interreligious dialogue or because of a certain reluctance to bear witness to their faith in Jesus Christ in contemporary society.

27. It is also important to consider the life itself of the ecclesial community, its internal quality. A first consideration is to discover how the fruits of the Second Vatican Council have been received and matured in the Church. The great conciliar documents have not been a dead letter: their effects are confirmed. The four constitutions—Sacrosanctum Concilium, Lumen Gentium, Dei Verbum and Gaudium et Spes—have fertilized the Church. In effect:

28. In the midst of this fruitfulness, "defects and difficulties in the reception of the Council" must also be recognized.( [+[0]+] ) Despite such a broad and profound ecclesiological doctrine, the sense of ecclesial belonging has been weakened; A "disaffection towards the Church" is frequently observed; ([+[1]+]) it is often seen unilaterally, as a mere institution, deprived of its mystery.
29. There are many positive aspects of catechesis in recent years, which show its vitality. Among them it is worth highlighting:
30. Some problems, however, must today be examined with particular care, trying to find solutions to them:

31. Having analyzed the land, the sower sends his workers to announce the Gospel throughout the world, communicating to them the power of his Spirit. At the same time, he shows them how to read the signs of the times and asks them to carefully prepare for sowing.

32. The voice of the Spirit that Jesus, on behalf of the Father, has sent to his disciples also resonates in the events of history themselves.( [+[0]+] ) After the changing data of the current situation, and in the deep motivations of the challenges that are presented to evangelization, it is necessary to discover "the signs of the presence and plan of God." ( [+[1]+] ) This is an analysis that must be done in the light of faith, with understanding attitude. Using the human sciences, ([+[2]+] ) always necessary, the Church tries to discover the meaning of the current situation within the history of salvation. Their judgments about reality are always diagnostic for the mission.
33. In order to express its vitality and effectiveness, catechesis must assume, today, the following challenges and options:

34. Jesus, after his resurrection, sent the Holy Spirit on behalf of the Father to carry out the work of salvation from within and encourage the disciples to continue their own mission in the entire world, as he in turn had been sent by the Father. He was the first and greatest evangelizer. He announced the Kingdom of God, ([+[0]+] ) as a new and definitive divine intervention in history, and defined this announcement as "the Gospel", that is, the good news. He dedicated his entire earthly existence to him: he made known the joy of belonging to the Kingdom, ( [+[1]+] ) its demands and its "magna carta", ( [+[2]+] ) the mysteries it contains, ( [+[3]+] ) the fraternal life of those who enter it, ( [+[4]+] ) and its future plenitude. ( [+[5]+] )
35. This first part tries to define the proper character of catechesis.

36. "God, creating and preserving the universe through his Word, offers men in creation a perennial testimony of himself."( [+[0]+] ) Man, who by his nature and vocation is "capable of God," when he listens to the message of creatures can reach the certainty of the existence of God as the cause and end of everything and that He can reveal himself to man.
37. This benevolent plan ( [+[0]+] ) of the Father, fully revealed in Jesus Christ, is carried out with the power of the Holy Spirit.

38. God, in his immensity, to reveal himself to the human person, uses pedagogy: ( [+[0]+] ) he uses human events and words to communicate his plan; and he does it progressively, in stages, ([+[1]+] ) to better get closer to men. God, in fact, works in such a way that men come to the knowledge of his saving plan through the events of salvation history and the divinely inspired words that accompany and explain them.

39. Evangelization, which transmits Revelation to the world, is also carried out with works and words. It is, at the same time, testimony and announcement, word and sacrament, teaching and commitment.
40. God progressively revealed himself to men, through prophets and saving events, until he completed his revelation by sending his own Son:( [+[0]+] )

41. The ministry of the Word must highlight this admirable characteristic, typical of the economy of Revelation: the Son of God enters the history of men, assumes human life and death and makes the new and definitive alliance between God and men. It is the proper task of catechesis to show who Jesus Christ is: his life and his mystery, and to present the Christian faith as a follow-up to his person.( [+[0]+] ) To do this, it must continually rely on the gospels, which "are the heart of all Scripture, as they are the main testimony of the life and doctrine of the Word made flesh, our Savior."( [+[1]+] )

42. The Revelation of God, culminated in Jesus Christ, is intended for all humanity: "God wants all men to be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth" ([+[0]+]). By virtue of this universal saving will, God has arranged that the Revelation be transmitted to all peoples, to all generations, and remain intact forever.( [+[1]+] )

43. To fulfill this divine plan, Jesus Christ established the Church on the foundation of the Apostles and, sending them the Holy Spirit on behalf of the Father, commanded them to preach the Gospel throughout the world. The Apostles, with words, works and writings, faithfully fulfilled this mandate.( [+[0]+] )

44. The entire preservation of Revelation, the Word of God contained in Tradition and in Scripture, as well as its continuous transmission, are guaranteed in its authenticity. The Magisterium of the Church, sustained by the Holy Spirit and endowed with the "charisma of truth", exercises the function of "authentically interpreting the Word of God".( [+[0]+] )

45. The Church, "universal sacrament of salvation",( [+[0]+] ) moved by the Holy Spirit, transmits Revelation through evangelization: it announces the good news of the Father's saving plan and, in the sacraments, communicates the divine gifts.
46. The Church "exists to evangelize", ([+[0]+]) that is, to "bring the Good News to all areas of humanity and, with its influence, transform from within, renew humanity itself." ( [+[1]+] )

47. The Church, although permanently containing within itself the fullness of the means of salvation, works gradually.( [+[0]+] ) The conciliar decree Ad Gentes has well clarified the dynamics of the evangelizing process: Christian witness, dialogue and presence of charity ( [+[1]+] ), announcement of the Gospel and call to conversion ( [+[2]+] ), catechumenate and Christian initiation ( [+[3]+] ), formation of the community Christian, through the sacraments, with its ministries ( [+[4]+] ). 113 This is the dynamism of the implantation and construction of the Church.
48. According to this, we must conceive evangelization as the process by which the Church, moved by the Spirit, announces and spreads the Gospel throughout the world, in such a way that it:

49. The evangelizing process, ( [+[0]+] ) therefore, is structured in stages or "essential moments": ( [+[1]+] ) missionary action for non-believers and for those who live in religious indifference; the catechetical-initiative action for those who choose the Gospel and for those who need to complete or restructure their initiation; and pastoral action for mature Christian faithful, within the Christian community. ( [+[2]+] ) These moments, however, are not closed stages: they are reiterated whenever necessary, since they try to provide the most appropriate evangelical nourishment for the spiritual growth of each person or of the community itself.

50. The ministry of the Word ( [+[0]+] ) is a fundamental element of evangelization. The Christian presence among different human groups and the testimony of life need to be clarified and justified by the explicit announcement of Jesus Christ, the Lord. "There is no true evangelization until the name, the doctrine, the life, the promises, the kingdom, the mystery of Jesus of Nazareth, Son of God, are announced." ( [+[1]+] ) Also those who are already disciples of Christ need to be constantly fed with the Word of God to grow in their Christian life. ( [+[2]+] )
51. The main functions of the ministry of the Word are the following:

52. Important forms of the ministry of the Word are: the first missionary announcement or preaching, pre- and post-baptismal catechesis, the liturgical form and the theological form. It often happens that such forms—due to pastoral circumstances—must assume more than one function. Catechesis, for example, along with its function of initiation, must frequently assume missionary tasks. The same homily, depending on the circumstances, should assume the functions of convocation and organic initiation.

53. Evangelization, by announcing to the world the Good News of Revelation, invites men and women to conversion and faith.( [+[0]+] ) The call of Jesus, "convert and believe the Gospel" ( [+[1]+] ), continues to resonate, today, through the evangelization of the Church.

54. This "yes" to Jesus Christ, the fullness of the Revelation of the Father, contains within itself a double dimension: confident surrender to God and cordial assent to everything He has revealed to us. This is only possible through the action of the Holy Spirit.( [+[0]+] )

55. Faith brings with it a change of life, a "metanoia", ( [+[0]+] ) that is, a profound transformation of the mind and heart: it thus makes the believer live that "new way of being, of living, of living together, which the Gospel inaugurates".( [+[1]+] ) And this change of life is manifested at all levels of the Christian's existence: in his interior life of adoration and acceptance of the divine will; in their active participation in the mission of the Church; in your marriage and family life; in the exercise of professional life; in the performance of economic and social activities.

56. Faith is a gift destined to grow in the hearts of believers. ( [+[0]+] ) Adhesion to Jesus Christ, in fact, gives rise to a permanent conversion process that lasts a lifetime. ( [+[1]+] ) Whoever comes to faith is like a newborn child ( [+[2]+] ) who, little by little, will grow and become an adult being, who tends to the "state of a perfect man", ( [+[3]+] ) to the maturity of the fullness of Christ.

57. The ministry of the Word is at the service of this process of full conversion. The first announcement has the character of calling to faith; catechesis is the foundation for conversion, basically structuring the Christian life; and the permanent education of the faith, in which the homily stands out, the character of being the constant food that every adult organism needs to live. ( [+[0]+] )

58. The evangelization of the world is faced with a very diversified and changing religious panorama, in which we can fundamentally distinguish "three situations" ([+[0]+]) that call for appropriate and differentiated responses.

59. These socio-religious situations are obviously different and it is not fair to equate them. Such diversity, which has always occurred in the mission of the Church, takes on something new today, in this changing world. In fact, they frequently live together in the same territory. In many large cities, for example, the situation that calls for a "mission ad gentes" and that which calls for a "new evangelization" coexist simultaneously. Along with them, Christian missionary communities are dynamically present, nourished by adequate "pastoral action." Today it is common that in the territory of a particular Church, it is necessary to attend to all of these situations. "It is not easy to define the borders between pastoral care for the faithful, new evangelization and specific missionary action, and it is not thinkable to create barriers or watertight compartments between them." 177 In fact, "each one influences the other, stimulates it and helps it." ( [+[0]+] )
60. This chapter shows the relationship of catechesis with the other elements of evangelization, of which it is an integral part.

61. The first announcement is addressed to non-believers and those who, in fact, live in religious indifference. It assumes the function of announcing the Gospel and calling for conversion. Catechesis, "different from the first proclamation of the Gospel", ([+[0]+]) promotes and matures this initial conversion, educating the convert in the faith and incorporating him into the Christian community. The relationship between both forms of the ministry of the Word is, therefore, a relationship of distinction in complementarity.

62. In pastoral practice, however, the boundaries between both actions are not easily delimitable. Frequently, people who access catechesis need, in fact, a true conversion. For this reason, the Church desires that, ordinarily, a first stage of the catechizing process be dedicated to ensuring conversion. ( [+[0]+] ) In the "mission ad gentes", this task is carried out in the "precatechumenate". ( [+[1]+] ) In the situation that requires the "new evangelization" it is carried out through "kerygmatic catechesis", which some call "pre-catechetics", ( [+[2]+] ) because, inspired by the precatechumenate, it is a proposal of the Good News in order to a solid option of faith. Only from conversion, and counting on the interior attitude of "the one who creates", catechesis itself will be able to develop its specific task of education of the faith. ( [+[3]+] )

63. The Apostolic Exhortation Catechesi Tradendae, when it places catechesis within the mission of the Church, remembers that evangelization is a rich, complex and dynamic reality, which includes essential and different "moments." And he adds: "Catechesis is one of those moments—and how important—in the total process of evangelization." ( [+[0]+] ) This means that there are actions that « prepare » ( [+[1]+] ) for catechesis and actions that « emanate » ( [+[2]+] ) from it.

64. Catechesis, by carrying out this function of initiation of the ministry of the Word in different ways, lays the foundations of the edifice of faith. ( [+[0]+] ) Other functions of that same ministry will later build the various floors of that same building.

65. Faith, by which man responds to the announcement of the Gospel, demands Baptism. The intimate relationship between the two realities has its roots in the will of Christ himself, who commanded his apostles to make disciples of all people and baptize them. "The mission of baptizing, therefore, the sacramental mission, is included in the mission of evangelizing." ( [+[0]+] )

66. Catechesis is, thus, a fundamental element of Christian initiation and is closely linked to the sacraments of initiation, especially Baptism, "sacrament of faith." ( [+[0]+] ) The link that unites catechesis with Baptism is the profession of faith, which is, at the same time, the interior element of this sacrament and the goal of catechesis. The purpose of catechetical action consists precisely in this: to promote a living, explicit and active profession of faith. ( [+[1]+] )
67. The fact of being an "essential moment" of the evangelizing process, at the service of Christian initiation, gives catechesis some characteristics: ( [+[0]+] )

68. In summary, initiation catechesis, because it is organic and systematic, is not reduced to what is merely circumstantial or occasional; ( [+[0]+] ) because it is training for the Christian life, it goes beyond—including it—mere teaching; ( [+[1]+] ) Because it is essential, it focuses on what is "common" for the Christian, without entering into disputed issues or becoming a theological investigation. In short, because it is an initiation, it incorporates the community that lives, celebrates and witnesses the faith. It therefore carries out, at the same time, tasks of initiation, education and instruction. ( [+[2]+] ) This richness, inherent in the catechumenate of unbaptized adults, must inspire other forms of catechesis.

69. Continuing education in the faith is subsequent to and presupposes basic education. Both update two functions of the ministry of the Word, different and complementary, at the service of the permanent process of conversion.

70. In the Christian community, the disciples of Jesus Christ are fed at a double table: "that of the Word of God and that of the Body of Christ." ( [+[0]+] ) The Gospel and the Eucharist are his constant nourishment on the pilgrimage to the Father's house. The action of the Holy Spirit causes the gift of "communion" and the commitment to "mission" to be deepened and lived in an ever more profound way.
71. For the permanent education of the faith, the ministry of the Word has many forms of catechesis. Among others, the following can be highlighted:

72. It is essential that the initiation catechesis of adults, baptized or not, the initiation catechesis of children and young people and the permanent catechesis are well linked to the catechetical project of the Christian community, so that the particular Church grows harmoniously, and its evangelizing activity flows from authentic sources. «It is important that the catechesis of children and young people, the permanent catechesis and the catechesis of adults are not watertight and incommunicative compartments... It is necessary to promote their perfect complementarity.» ( [+[0]+] )
73. A special consideration deserves, within the ministry of the Word, the character of school religious education and its relationship with the catechesis of children and young people.

74. School religious education is developed in diverse school contexts, which means that, while maintaining its own character, it also acquires diverse accents. These accents depend on the legal and organizational conditions, the didactic conception, the personal budgets of educators and students, and the relationship between school religious teaching and family and parish catechesis.

75. The life and faith situation of students who attend school religious education is characterized by notable and continuous instability. School religious teaching must take into account this changing reality in order to achieve its purpose.

76. Family Christian education, catechesis and school religious teaching, each in its own way, are closely related within the service of Christian education for children, adolescents and young people. In practice, however, different variable elements must be taken into account, which are occasionally presented, in order to proceed with realism and pastoral prudence in the application of the general guidelines.

77. Having clarified the place that catechesis occupies within the evangelizing mission of the Church, as well as its relationships with the other elements of evangelization and with other forms of the ministry of the Word, this chapter seeks to reflect specifically on:

78. Catechesis is an essentially ecclesial action. ( [+[0]+] ) The true subject of catechesis is the Church which, as continuer of the mission of Jesus Christ the Master and animated by the Spirit, has been sent to be a teacher of the faith. For this reason, the Church, imitating the Mother of the Lord, faithfully preserves the Gospel in its heart, ( [+[1]+] ) announces it, celebrates it, lives it and transmits it in catechesis to all those who have decided to follow Jesus Christ.

79. The Church, by transmitting - in Christian initiation - faith and new life, acts as a mother of men, who generates children conceived by the work of the Holy Spirit and born of God. ( [+[0]+] ) Precisely, "because she is a mother, she is also the educator of our faith"; ( [+[1]+] ) is a mother and a teacher, at the same time. Through catechesis he feeds his children with his own faith and inserts them, as members, into the ecclesial family. As a good mother, she offers them the Gospel in all its authenticity and purity, which is given to them, at the same time, as adapted, culturally enriched food and as a response to the deepest aspirations of the human heart.
80. "The definitive goal of catechesis is to put one not only in contact but in communion, in intimacy with Jesus Christ." ( [+[0]+] )

81. Communion with Jesus Christ, by its own dynamic, impels the disciple to unite with everything with which Jesus Christ himself was deeply united: with God, his Father, who had sent him to the world and with the Holy Spirit, who impelled him to the mission; with the Church, his Body, for which he gave himself; with the men, his brothers, whose fate he wanted to share.

82. Catechesis is that particular form of the ministry of the Word that matures the initial conversion until it becomes a living, explicit and operative confession of faith: "Catechesis has its origin in the confession of faith and leads to the confession of faith." ( [+[0]+] )

83. The profession of faith is only full if it is referred to the Church. Every baptized person proclaims the Creed in the singular, since no action is more personal than this. But he recites it in and through the Church, since he does so as a member of it. The "I believe" and the "we believe" imply each other. ( [+[0]+] ) By merging his confession with that of the Church, the Christian joins the latter's mission: to be a "universal sacrament of salvation" for the life of the world. He who proclaims the profession of faith assumes commitments that, not infrequently, will attract persecution. In Christian history, martyrs are the announcers and witnesses par excellence. ( [+[1]+] )

84. The purpose of catechesis is achieved through various tasks, mutually involved. ( [+[0]+] ) To update them, catechesis will certainly be inspired by the way in which Jesus formed his disciples: he made them aware of the different dimensions of the Kingdom of God ( [+[1]+] ), ( [+[2]+] ) he taught them to pray ( [+[3]+] ), ( [+[4]+] ) he instilled in them evangelical attitudes ( [+[5]+] ). ( [+[6]+] )

contenido: 85. The fundamental tasks of catechesis are:

86. Catechesis enables the Christian to live in community and to actively participate in the life and mission of the Church. The Second Vatican Council points out to pastors the need to "properly cultivate the spirit of community" ([+[0]+]) and to catechumens the need to "learn to cooperate effectively in the evangelization and edification of the Church." ( [+[1]+] )
87. The tasks of catechesis constitute, consequently, a rich and varied set of aspects. Several considerations should be made regarding this set:

88. Faith, driven by divine grace and cultivated by the action of the Church, undergoes a process of maturation. Catechesis, at the service of this growth, is a gradual action. Appropriate catechesis is arranged by grades. ( [+[0]+] )

89. These stages, full of the wisdom of the great catechumenal tradition, inspire the gradualness of catechesis. ( [+[0]+] ) In the time of the Fathers of the Church, in fact, catechumenal formation was carried out through biblical catechesis, centered on the narration of the History of Salvation; the immediate preparation for Baptism, through a doctrinal catechesis, which explained the Symbol and the Lord's Prayer, recently delivered, with their moral implications; and the stage that followed the sacraments of initiation, through a mystagogic catechesis, which helped to internalize them and incorporate them into the community. This patristic conception continues to be a focus of light for the current catechumenate and for the initiation catechesis itself.

90. Since the "mission ad gentes" is the paradigm of all the missionary action of the Church, the baptismal catechumenate inherent to it is the inspiring model of its catechizing action. ( [+[0]+] ) Therefore, it is convenient to underline the elements of the catechumenate that should inspire current catechesis and the meaning of this inspiration.
91. Assuming this essential difference, some elements of the baptismal catechumenate are now considered, which should be a source of inspiration for post-baptismal catechesis:
92. The Christian faith, by which a person says "yes" to Jesus Christ, can be considered in two aspects:
93. This second part deals with the content of the evangelical message ([+[0]+]).
94. The source from which catechesis takes its message is the Word of God itself:
95. The Word of God contained in Sacred Tradition and Sacred Scripture:

96. All of these are the main or subsidiary sources of catechesis, which in no way should be taken in a univocal sense. ( [+[0]+] ) Holy Scripture "is the Word of God in that, by inspiration of the Holy Spirit, it is recorded in writing"; ( [+[1]+] ) and Sacred Tradition "transmits in its entirety to the successors of the apostles the Word of God that was entrusted to them by Christ the Lord and by the Holy Spirit." ( [+[2]+] ) The Magisterium has the function of "authentically interpreting the Word of God", ( [+[3]+] ) carrying out - in the name of Jesus Christ - a fundamental ecclesial service. Tradition, Scripture and Magisterium, closely intertwined and united, are, "each in their own way", ([+[4]+]) main sources of catechesis.
97. The criteria for presenting the evangelical message in catechesis are closely related to each other, since they spring from a single source.
98. Jesus Christ not only transmits the Word of God: He is the Word of God. Therefore, catechesis—all of it—is referred to Him.

99. The Word of God, incarnated in Jesus of Nazareth, Son of the Virgin Mary, is the Word of the Father, who speaks to the world through his Spirit. Jesus constantly refers to the Father, of whom He knows He is the Only Son, and to the Holy Spirit, by whom He knows He is the Anointed One. He is the "way" that leads into the intimate mystery of God. ( [+[0]+] )
100. The Trinitarian Christocentrism of the evangelical message impels catechesis to take care, among others, of the following aspects:

101. Jesus' message about God is good news for humanity. Jesus, in effect, announced the Kingdom of God: ( [+[0]+] ) a new and definitive divine intervention, with a transforming power as great, and even greater, than the one he used in the creation of the world. ( [+[1]+] ) In this sense, "as the nucleus and center of the Good News, Christ announces salvation: that great gift of God that is liberation from everything that oppresses man, but above all it is liberation from sin and evil, within the joy of knowing God and being known by Him, of seeing Him, of surrendering to Him." ( [+[2]+] )
102. In this explanation of the evangelical kerygma of Jesus, catechesis highlights the following fundamental aspects:

103. The Good News of the Kingdom of God, which announces salvation, includes a message of liberation. ( [+[0]+] ) In announcing this Kingdom, Jesus addressed the poor in a very particular way: “Blessed are the poor, for yours is the Kingdom of God. Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be satisfied. Blessed are you who cry now, for you will laugh » ( [+[1]+] ). These beatitudes of Jesus, addressed to those who suffer, are an eschatological announcement of the salvation that the Kingdom brings with it. They point to that lacerating experience to which the Gospel is so sensitive: poverty, hunger and the suffering of humanity.
104. To prepare Christians for this task, catechesis will take care, among others, of the following aspects:

105. The ecclesial nature of catechesis gives the evangelical message it transmits an intrinsic ecclesial character. Catechesis has its origin in the confession of faith of the Church and leads to the confession of faith of the catechumen and the catechist. The first official word that the Church addresses to the baptized adult, after inquiring about his or her name, is to ask him: "What do you ask of the Church of God?" ». «Faith», is the candidate's response. ( [+[0]+] ) The catechumen knows, in fact, that the Gospel that he has discovered and wishes to know is alive in the hearts of believers. Catechesis is nothing other than the process of transmitting the Gospel as the Christian community has received it, understands it, celebrates it, lives it and communicates it in multiple ways.

106. This faith, transmitted by the ecclesial community, is one. Although the disciples of Jesus Christ form a community dispersed throughout the world and although catechesis transmits the faith in very different cultural languages, the Gospel that is delivered is only one, the confession of faith is only one and only one Baptism: "one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God and Father of all" ([+[0]+]).

107. The confession of faith of the disciples of Jesus Christ springs from a pilgrim Church, sent on mission. It is not yet the glorious proclamation of the end of the road, but rather the one that corresponds to the "time of the Church." ( [+[0]+] ) The "economy of salvation" has a historical character, since it is carried out in time: "it began in the past, it developed and reached its summit in Christ; He displays his power in the present; and awaits its consummation in the future. ( [+[1]+] )
108. The historical character of the Christian message obliges catechesis to take care of these aspects:

109. The Word of God became man, a concrete man, situated in time and space, rooted in a specific culture: "Christ, through his incarnation, united himself with the concrete social and cultural conditions of the men with whom he lived." ( [+[0]+] ) This is the original "inculturation" of the Word of God and the referential model for all the evangelization of the Church, "called to bring the force of the Gospel to the heart of culture and cultures." ( [+[1]+] )
110. In this inculturation of the faith, catechesis is specifically presented with various tasks. Among them it is worth highlighting:

111. In the task of inculturation of the faith, catechesis must transmit the evangelical message in all its integrity and purity. Jesus announces the Gospel in its entirety: "Everything I have heard from my Father I have made known to you" ([+[0]+]). And this same integrity is required by Christ of his disciples, when sending them on the mission: "Teach them to observe everything that I have commanded you" ([+[1]+]). For this reason, a fundamental criterion of catechesis is to safeguard the integrity of the message, avoiding partial or distorted presentations of it: "In order for the "oblation of his faith" to be perfect, he who becomes a disciple of Christ has the right to receive the "word of faith" not mutilated, falsified or diminished, but complete and integral, in all its rigor and vigor. " ( [+[2]+] )
112. Two closely linked dimensions underlie this criterion. It is, in effect:

113. In this complex relationship between inculturation and integrity of the Christian message, the criterion that must be followed is that of an evangelical attitude of "missionary openness for the integral salvation of the world." ( [+[0]+] ) This attitude must know how to combine the acceptance of truly human and religious values, above immobile closures, with the missionary commitment to announce all the truth of the gospel, above easy accommodations that would lead to distorting the Gospel and secularizing the Church. Evangelical authenticity excludes both attitudes, contrary to the true meaning of the mission.

114. The message transmitted by catechesis has "an organic and hierarchical character", ([+[0]+]) constituting a coherent and vital synthesis of the faith. It is organized around the mystery of the Holy Trinity, in a Christ-centered perspective, since this mystery is "the source of all the other mysteries of faith and the light that illuminates them." ( [+[1]+] ) From there, the harmony of the whole message requires a "hierarchy of truths", ( [+[2]+] ) because the connection of each of them with the foundation of the Christian faith is diverse. Now "this hierarchy does not mean that some truths belong to the faith less than others, but rather that some truths rely on others as more important and are illuminated by them." ( [+[3]+] )
115. All aspects and dimensions of the Christian message participate in this hierarchical organicity:

116. The Word of God, upon becoming man, assumes human nature in everything except sin. In this way, Jesus Christ, who is "the image of the invisible God" ([+[0]+]), is also the perfect man. Hence "in reality, the mystery of man is only clarified in the mystery of the incarnate Word." ( [+[1]+] )

117. For this reason, eminently Christological, catechesis, when presenting the Christian message, "must be concerned with directing men's attention towards their most important experiences, both personal and social, its task being to raise, in the light of the Gospel, the questions that arise from them, so as to stimulate the just desire to transform one's own conduct." ( [+[0]+] ) In this sense:

118. The norms and criteria indicated in this chapter and "which belong to the exposition of the content of catechesis, must be applied in the different forms of catechesis: that is, in biblical and liturgical catechesis, in the doctrinal summary, in the interpretation of the situations of human existence, etc. ». ( [+[0]+] )
119. This chapter reflects on the content of catechesis as the Church exposes it in the syntheses of faith that it officially elaborates and proposes in its Catechisms.
120. The Catechism of the Catholic Church and the General Directory for Catechesis are two different and complementary instruments, at the service of the catechizing action of the Church:

121. The Catechism of the Catholic Church itself indicates, in its prologue, the purpose it pursues: "This catechism aims to present an organic and synthetic exposition of the essential and fundamental contents of Catholic doctrine, both on faith and morals, in the light of the Second Vatican Council and the entire Tradition of the Church." ( [+[0]+] )

122. The Catechism of the Catholic Church is articulated around four fundamental dimensions of Christian life: the profession of faith, the liturgical celebration, evangelical morality and prayer. All four spring from the same core, the Christian mystery, which:
123. The central axis of the Catechism of the Catholic Church is Jesus Christ, "way, truth and life" ([+[0]+]).

124. It is important to discover the literary genre of the Catechism of the Catholic Church to respect the function that the authority of the Church attributes to it in the exercise and renewal of catechetical activity in our time.

125. The Second Vatican Council set itself the main task of safeguarding and better explaining the precious deposit of Christian doctrine, in order to make it more accessible to the faithful of Christ and to all men of good will.
126. In light of this relationship of the Catechism of the Catholic Church regarding the deposit of faith, it is appropriate to clarify two issues of vital importance for catechesis:

127. The Constitution Dei Verbum of the Second Vatican Council underlines the fundamental importance of Sacred Scripture in the life of the Church. The Holy Scripture is presented, together with the Sacred Tradition, "as the supreme rule of faith", since it "immutably transmits the word of God himself and, in the words of the Apostles and Prophets, makes the voice of the Holy Spirit resound." ( [+[0]+] ) That is why the Church wants that, in the entire ministry of the Word, the Holy Scripture has a preeminent position. Catechesis, in particular, must be "an authentic introduction to 'lectio divina', that is, to the reading of the Holy Scripture, done according to the Spirit who dwells in the Church." ( [+[1]+] )
128. The Sacred Scripture and the Catechism of the Catholic Church are presented as two points of reference to inspire all the catechizing action of the Church in our time:

129. In the "deposit of faith", together with Scripture, the entire Tradition of the Church is contained. "The sayings of the Holy Fathers attest to the life-giving presence of this Tradition, whose riches are infused into the practice and life of the believing and praying Church." ( [+[0]+] )

130. The Catechism of the Catholic Church, for its part, contributes to catechesis the great tradition of catechisms. ( [+[0]+] ) Of the great richness of this tradition, here too some aspects deserve to be highlighted:

131. The Catechism of the Catholic Church is offered to all the faithful and to every man who wants to know what the Church believes; ( [+[0]+] ) and, in a very particular way, "it is intended to encourage and facilitate the writing of new local catechisms that take into account diverse situations and cultures, but that carefully maintain the unity of faith and fidelity to Catholic doctrine." ( [+[1]+] )

132. Three main features characterize every catechism, assumed to be typical of a local Church: its official character, the organic and basic synthesis of the faith it offers and the fact that it is offered, together with Sacred Scripture, as a point of reference for catechesis.

133. The Catechism of the Catholic Church indicates which aspects must be taken into account when adapting or contextualizing the organic synthesis of the faith that every local Catechism must offer. This synthesis of faith must respond to the demands that arise from "the different cultures, ages, spiritual life, social and ecclesial situations of those to whom catechesis is directed." ( [+[0]+] ) The Second Vatican Council also emphatically affirms the need to adapt the evangelical message: "This adapted preaching of the revealed word must be maintained as the law of all evangelization." ( [+[1]+] ) According to this:

134. Local Churches, in the task of adapting, contextualizing and inculturating the Gospel message to different ages, situations and cultures, through Catechisms, need accurate and mature creativity. From the depositum fidei, entrusted to the Church, local Churches must select, structure and express, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, the inner Teacher, all those elements with which to transmit, in a given situation, the Gospel in all its authenticity.
135. In the preparation of local Catechisms it is worth remembering the following:

136. The Catechism of the Catholic Church and the local Catechisms, naturally with the specific authority of each one, form a unity. They are the concrete expression of "unity in the same apostolic faith" ([+[0]+]) and, at the same time, of the rich diversity of the formulation of that same faith.

137. Jesus carefully took care of the training of the disciples he sent on a mission. He presented himself to them as the only Teacher and at the same time patient and faithful friend; ( [+[0]+] ) his entire life was a continuous teaching; ( [+[1]+] ) stimulating them with appropriate questions ( [+[2]+] ) explained to them in a more profound way what he announced to the people; ( [+[3]+] ) initiated them into prayer; ( [+[4]+] ) sent them two by two to prepare for the mission; ( [+[5]+] ) He first promised them and then sent the Spirit of the Father to guide them to the full truth ( [+[6]+] ) and sustain them in the inevitable moments of difficulty. ( [+[7]+] ) Jesus Christ is « the Teacher who reveals God to men and man to himself; the Master who saves, sanctifies and guides, who is alive, who speaks, demands, who moves, who straightens, judges, forgives, walks daily with us in history; the Master who is coming and who will come in glory." ( [+[8]+] ) In Jesus Christ, Lord and Master, the Church finds transcendent grace, permanent inspiration, the convincing model for all communication of faith.

138. In the school of Jesus the Master, the catechist closely unites his action as a responsible person with the mysterious action of God's grace. Catechesis is, therefore, an exercise of an "original pedagogy of faith." ( [+[0]+] )

139. «God treats you like children; And what son is there whose father does not correct him? » ( [+[0]+] ). The salvation of the person, which is the goal of revelation, is also manifested as the fruit of an original and effective "pedagogy of God" throughout history. In analogy with human customs and according to the cultural categories of each time, Sacred Scripture presents God as a merciful father, a teacher, a wise man ( [+[1]+] ) who takes charge of the person - individual and community - in the conditions in which he finds himself, frees him from the bonds of evil, draws him to himself with ties of love, makes him grow progressively and patiently towards the maturity of a free son, faithful and obedient to his word. To this end, as a brilliant and far-sighted educator, God transforms the events of his people's lives into lessons of wisdom ( [+[2]+] ) adapting to different ages and life situations. Through instruction and catechesis, he places in his hands a message that is transmitted from generation to generation, ( [+[3]+] ) corrects him by reminding him of the reward and punishment, he converts the same trials and sufferings into formative ones. ( [+[4]+] ) In reality, promoting a person's encounter with God, which is the task of the catechist, means putting the relationship that God has with the person at the center and making one's own and letting oneself be guided by Him.

140. When the fullness of time had arrived, God sent his Son, Jesus Christ, to humanity. He gave the world the supreme gift of salvation, carrying out his redemptive mission through a process that continued the "pedagogy of God", with the perfection and effectiveness inherent in the newness of his person. With the words, signs, and works of Jesus, throughout his brief but intense life, the disciples had direct experience of the fundamental features of the "pedagogy of Jesus", later recording them in the gospels: the welcome of the other, especially the poor, the little one, the sinner as a person loved and sought after by God; the genuine announcement of the Kingdom of God as good news of the truth and mercy of the Father; a style of tender and strong love that liberates from evil and promotes life; the compelling invitation to a way of living sustained by faith in God, hope in the Kingdom and charity towards one's neighbor; the use of all the resources of interpersonal communication, such as words, silence, metaphor, image, example, and many other signs, as was common in the biblical prophets. Inviting the disciples to follow him totally and unconditionally, ( [+[0]+] ) Christ teaches them the pedagogy of faith to the extent that they fully share his mission and destiny.

141. From its beginnings the Church, which is "in Christ as a sacrament", ( [+[0]+] ) lives its mission in visible and current continuity with the pedagogy of the Father and the Son. She, "being our Mother, is also an educator of our faith." ( [+[1]+] )

142. "Blessed is the man whom you correct, Yahweh, whom you instruct with your law." catechesis and the contributions of science and experience. ( [+[2]+] ) In this way, knowing more and more the mystery of salvation, learning to adore God the Father and "being sincere in love", he tries to "grow in everything towards Him who is the head, Christ" ( [+[3]+] ).

143. Catechesis, as the communication of divine Revelation, is radically inspired by the pedagogy of God as it is carried out in Christ and in the Church, takes its constitutive lines from it and, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, develops a wise synthesis of that pedagogy, thus promoting a true experience of faith and a filial encounter with God. In this way catechesis:

144. Catechesis, which is therefore pedagogy in an act of faith, when carrying out its tasks, cannot be inspired by ideological considerations or by merely human interests; ( [+[0]+] ) does not confuse the saving action of God, which is pure grace, with the pedagogical action of man, but neither does it contrast and separate them. The dialogue that God lovingly maintains with each person becomes his inspiration and norm; Of this dialogue, catechesis is a tireless "echo", constantly seeking dialogue with people, according to the fundamental indications offered by the Magisterium of the Church. ( [+[1]+] )

145. Jesus Christ constitutes the living and perfect relationship of God with man and of man with God. From Him the pedagogy of faith receives "a fundamental law for the entire life of the Church ([+[0]+]): fidelity to God and man, in the same attitude of love." ( [+[1]+] )

contenido: 146. Wanting to speak to men as friends, ( [+[0]+] ) God manifests his pedagogy in a particular way by adapting his way of speaking with solicitous providence to our earthly condition. ( [+[1]+] )

147. Continuously inspired by the pedagogy of faith, the catechist configures a service as a qualified educational itinerary; That is to say, on the one hand, it helps the person to open up to the religious dimension of life, and on the other hand, it proposes the Gospel in such a way that it penetrates and transforms the processes of understanding, conscience, freedom and action, so that existence becomes a gift of self to the example of Jesus Christ.

148. In the transmission of the faith, the Church does not have its own or unique method, but rather, in the light of God's pedagogy, it discerns the methods of each era, assumes with freedom of spirit "everything that is true, noble, just, pure, lovely, honorable, everything that is virtue and something worthy of praise" ([+[0]+]), in short, all the elements that are not contrary to the Gospel, and puts them at its service. This is admirably confirmed by the history of the Church, in which numerous charismas of service to the Word of God have given rise to very diverse methods. In this way, "variety in methods is a sign of life and richness", and at the same time a sign of respect for the recipients. Such variety is required by "the age and intellectual development of Christians, their degree of ecclesial and spiritual maturity and many other personal circumstances." ( [+[1]+] )

149. The principle of "fidelity to God and fidelity to man" leads to the avoidance of any contrast, artificial separation or presumed neutrality between method and content, rather affirming their necessary correlation and interaction. The catechist recognizes that the method is at the service of revelation and conversion, ([+[0]+]) and that is why he must use it. On the other hand, the catechist knows that the content of catechesis is not indifferent to any method, but requires a transmission process appropriate to the nature of the message, its sources and languages, the concrete circumstances of the ecclesial community, and the condition of each of the faithful to whom the catechesis is directed.

150. The communication of faith in catechesis is an event of grace, carried out by the encounter of the Word of God with the experience of the person, which is expressed through sensitive signs and finally opens to the mystery. It can happen in various ways that we do not always fully know.

151. On the other hand, when reference is made to operational itineraries, another meaning can be given: one is also called "kerygmatic" ([+[0]+]), which starts from the announcement of the message, expressed in the main documents of faith ([+[1]+]) and applies them to life; the other, called "existential" ([+[2]+]), which starts from human problems and situations and illuminates them with the light of the Word of God. In themselves, they are legitimate modes of access if all the factors at play are respected, the mystery of grace and the human fact, the understanding of faith and the process of rationality.
152. Experience exercises various functions in catechesis, in the light of which existence itself must always be duly valued.

153. The illumination and interpretation of experience in the light of faith becomes a permanent task of catechetical pedagogy, not free from difficulties, but which cannot be neglected, under penalty of falling into artificial juxtapositions or reductionist understandings of the truth.

154. Catechesis is linked to the "Memory" of the Church that keeps the presence of the Lord alive among us. ( [+[0]+] ) The exercise of memory is, therefore, a constitutive element of the pedagogy of faith, since the beginnings of Christianity. To overcome the risks of mechanical memorization, the exercise of memory must be harmoniously integrated between the various functions of learning, such as spontaneity and reflection, moments of dialogue and silence, oral communication and written work. ( [+[1]+] )

155. In even greater depth, the learning of the formulas of faith and its believing profession must be understood within the framework of the traditional and valid exercise of "traditio" and "redditio", thanks to which, the delivery of faith in catechesis ([+[0]+]) corresponds to man's response throughout the catechetical path and later in life ([+[1]+]). ( [+[2]+] )
156. No method, no matter how experienced, exempts the catechist from personal work in any of the phases of the catechesis process.

157. Active participation in the formative process of those being catechized is in full conformity, not only with true human communication, but especially with the economy of revelation and salvation. In fact, in ordinary Christian life, believers are called to respond actively, personally and in groups, to the gift of God through prayer, participation in the sacraments and other liturgical actions, ecclesial and social commitment, the exercise of charity, the promotion of great human values, such as freedom, justice, peace, and the safeguarding of creation.

158. Catechetical pedagogy is effective to the extent that the Christian community becomes a concrete and exemplary reference for each person's journey of faith. This happens if the community is conceived as the source, place and goal of catechesis. Specifically, the community becomes a visible place of testimony of faith, takes care of the formation of its members, welcomes them as the family of God, becoming a vital and permanent environment for the growth of faith. ( [+[0]+] )

159. The group has an important function in the development processes of the person. This also applies to catechesis, in that of the little ones because it promotes good socialization; in that of young people for whom the group is almost a vital necessity in the formation of their personality; and in that of adults because it promotes a style of dialogue, cooperation and Christian co-responsibility.

160. «The first Areopagus of modern times is the world of communication, which is unifying humanity... Social media have achieved such importance that for many they are the main information and training instrument, of guidance and inspiration for individual, family and social behavior.» ( [+[0]+] ) For this reason, along with the numerous traditional media in force, "the use of mass media has become essential for evangelization and catechesis." ( [+[1]+] ) Indeed, "the Church would feel guilty before her Lord if she did not use those powerful means, which human intelligence perfects more and more...in them the Church finds a modern and effective version of the pulpit. Thanks to them he can speak to the masses. ( [+[2]+] )

161. The correct use of these means requires catechists to make a serious effort of knowledge, competence and qualified updating. But above all, given the great influence that these media exert on culture, we must not forget that "it is not enough to use them to spread the Christian message and the teaching of the Church, but it is important to integrate the message itself into this new culture created by modern communication... with new languages, new techniques and new psychological behaviors." ( [+[0]+] ) Only in this way, with the grace of God, does the evangelical message have the capacity to penetrate the conscience of each person and obtain "a truly personal adhesion and commitment in their favor." ( [+[1]+] )

162. All people related to these media, professionals and users, must be able to receive the grace of the Gospel. This should encourage catechists to consider different possibilities according to different people: media professionals, to whom to show the Gospel as a horizon of truth, responsibility, and inspiration; families—so exposed to the influence of the media—to protect them and, above all, help them acquire greater critical and educational capacity; ( [+[0]+] ) the young generations, as users and protagonists of mass-media communication. Everyone must be reminded that "in the use and reception of communication instruments, there is an urgent need for both an educational work of a critical sense, animated by the passion for the truth, and a work of defense of freedom, respect for the dignity of the person, and the elevation of the authentic culture of the people." ( [+[1]+] )

163. At the beginning of his ministry, Jesus proclaims that he has been sent to announce the good news to the poor, ( [+[0]+] ) implying, and later confirming it with his life, that the Kingdom of God is destined for all men, primarily those most in need. In fact, He becomes a catechist of the Kingdom of God for all kinds of people, old and small, rich and poor, healthy and sick, close and distant, Jews and pagans, men and women, just and sinners, people and authorities, individuals and groups... He shows himself available to each person and is interested in the needs of each one: those of the soul and those of the body, healing and forgiving, correcting and encouraging, with words and deeds.

164. This is the mission that the Church has carried out for two thousand years, with an immense variety of modalities of proclamation and catechesis, continually urged by the Spirit of Pentecost to reach with the Gospel "the Greeks and the barbarians, the wise and the ignorant" ([+[0]+]).

165. The necessary attention to the different and varied situations of people ( [+[0]+] ) drives catechesis to travel multiple paths to meet them and adapt the Christian message and the pedagogy of faith to their diverse needs. ( [+[1]+] )
166. Since it is not possible to deal in detail with each of the possible types of catechesis, only some aspects relevant to any situation are considered in this part:

167. Every baptized person, because he or she is called by God to maturity of faith, has the need and, therefore, the right to adequate catechesis. Therefore, the Church has the primary duty to respond in a convenient and satisfactory manner. In this sense we must remember, above all, that the recipient of the Gospel is "the concrete, historical man", ([+[0]+]) rooted in a given situation and influenced by certain psychological, social, cultural and religious conditions, whether he is aware of it or not. ( [+[1]+] )

168. Attention to each person should not make us forget, however, that catechesis is addressed to the Christian community as such and to each of its members in particular. If, in reality, catechesis receives legitimacy and strength from the life of the Church, it is also true that "the interior growth of the Church, its correspondence with God's plan, essentially depends on catechesis." ( [+[0]+] )

169. The "accommodating preaching of the revealed Word must be maintained as the law of all evangelization." ( [+[0]+] ) This norm has its intrinsic theological motivation in the mystery of the incarnation, corresponds to an elementary pedagogical requirement of healthy human communication, and reflects the practice of the Church throughout the centuries.

170. Adaptation is made according to the various circumstances in which the Word of God is transmitted. 558 It responds to "the demands that arise from the different cultures, ages, spiritual life, social and ecclesial situations of those to whom catechesis is directed." ( [+[0]+] ) Careful consideration should be given to them.

263. Base ecclesial communities have spread greatly in recent decades. ( [+[0]+] ) They are Christian groups that “are born from the need to live the life of the Church even more intensely; or the desire and search for a more human dimension, which the largest ecclesial communities can hardly offer... ». ( [+[1]+] )
264. A very fruitful catechesis can be developed in basic ecclesial communities:

265. The organization of catechetical pastoral care has as its point of reference the bishop and the diocese. The diocesan Secretariat of Catechesis ([+[0]+]) is "an instrument used by the bishop, head of the community and teacher of doctrine, to direct and guide all the catechetical activities of the diocese." ( [+[1]+] )
266. The main tasks of the diocesan Secretariat of Catechesis are the following:

267. To carry out these tasks, the Secretariat of Catechesis must have “a group of people endowed with specific competence. The breadth and variety of the issues to be dealt with require the distribution of responsibilities among several truly specialist people. ( [+[0]+] ) It is appropriate that this diocesan service be made up, ordinarily, of priests, religious and lay people.

268. In our time, this collaboration is extraordinarily fruitful. Reasons not only of geographical proximity but also of cultural homogeneity make common catechetical work advisable. "It is advisable that several dioceses unite their action, contributing for the common benefit experiences and projects, services and resources, so that the best equipped dioceses help the others and a common action program appears that reaches the entire region." ( [+[0]+] )
269. "Within the Episcopal Conference, a Secretariat or Catechetical Center ([+[0]+]) may be established, whose main task will be to help each diocese in matters of catechesis." ( [+[1]+] )

270. "Christ's mandate to announce the Gospel to every creature refers first of all and immediately to the Bishops with Peter and under the guidance of Peter." ( [+[0]+] ) In this collegial commission of Jesus, in order to announce and transmit the Gospel, the ministry of the Successor of Peter plays a fundamental role. This ministry, in fact, must be seen "not only as a global service that reaches the entire Church from the outside, but as belonging to the essence of each particular Church from within." ( [+[1]+] )

272. The coordination of catechesis is an important task in a particular Church. Two aspects can be considered in this coordination:
273. This section considers:

274. The diocesan catechetical project is the global catechetical offer of a particular Church that integrates, in an articulated, coherent and coordinated manner, the different catechetical processes offered by the diocese to recipients of different ages of life. ( [+[0]+] )

275. These various catechetical processes, each with possible socio-cultural variants, should not be organized separately, as if they were "watertight behaviors incommunicated with each other." ( [+[0]+] ) It is necessary that the catechetical offer of the particular Church be well coordinated. Among these various forms of catechesis "it is necessary to promote their perfect complementarity." ( [+[1]+] )

276. When defining catechesis as a moment in the total process of evangelization, the problem of coordinating catechetical action with the missionary action that precedes it, and with the pastoral action that continues it, necessarily arises. There are, in fact, elements "that prepare catechesis or emanate from it." ( [+[0]+] )

277. The current situation of evangelization postulates that the two actions, the missionary proclamation and the initiation catechesis, be conceived in coordination and offered, in the particular Church, through a unitary missionary and catechumenal evangelizing project. Today catechesis must be seen, above all, as the consequence of an effective missionary proclamation. The reference of the Ad Gentes decree, which places the catechumenate in the context of the missionary action of the Church, is a very valid reference criterion for all catechesis. ( [+[0]+] )

278. The educational ministry in the particular Church must establish the necessary coordination between the different "places" where education in the faith is carried out. It is very convenient that all these catechetical channels "truly converge towards the same confession of faith, towards the same belonging to the Church and towards commitments in society lived in the same evangelical spirit." ( [+[0]+] )

279. The particular Church, when trying to organize catechetical action, must start from an analysis of the situation. «The object of this research is multiple, since it covers the examination of pastoral action and the analysis of the religious situation, as well as the sociological, cultural and economic conditions, while these data from collective life can have a great influence on the process of evangelization.» ( [+[0]+] ) It is about becoming aware of reality, in relation to catechesis and its needs.

280. The analysis of the situation, at all these levels, «must convince those who exercise the ministry of the Word, that human situations are ambiguous with regard to pastoral action. It is necessary, therefore, that the workers of the Gospel learn to discover the possibilities open to their action in a new and diverse situation... A process of transformation is always possible that allows us to open a path to faith. ( [+[0]+] )

281. Once the situation has been carefully examined, it is necessary to proceed to the development of an action program. This program determines the objectives, the means of catechetical pastoral care and the norms that guide it, so that they respond perfectly to local needs, and are in full harmony with the objectives and norms of the universal Church.

282. Along with the action program, more focused on operational options, various Episcopates develop, at the national level, instruments of a more reflective and guiding nature, which provide the criteria for an ideal and adequate catechesis. They are called in various ways: Catechetical Directory, Catechetical Guidelines, Basic Document, Reference Text... Preferably intended for leaders and catechists, they try to clarify what catechesis consists of: its nature, purpose, tasks, contents, recipients, method. These Directories, or texts of general guidelines established by the Episcopal Conferences or issued under their authority, must follow the same process of preparation and approval provided for the Catechisms. Before being promulgated, they must be submitted to the approval of the Holy See. ( [+[0]+] )

283. Along with the instruments dedicated to guiding and planning the entire catechetical action ( [+[0]+] ) are the work instruments for immediate use, which are used within the catechetical act itself. First of all, there are the didactic texts ( [+[1]+] ) that are placed directly in the hands of the catechumens and those being catechized. And along with them are also the guides for catechists and, in the case of children's catechesis, for parents. ( [+[2]+] ) Likewise, the audiovisual media used in catechesis are important and on which appropriate discernment must be exercised. ( [+[3]+] )

contenido: 284. Within the set of instruments for catechesis, the Catechisms stand out. ( [+[0]+] ) Their importance derives from the fact that the message they transmit is recognized as authentic and proper by the pastors of the Church.

285. The "prior approval of the Apostolic See" ([+[0]+]) - which is required for the Catechisms emanating from the Episcopal Conferences - is understood, since they are documents through which the universal Church, in the different socio-cultural spaces to which it is sent, announces and transmits the Gospel and gives birth to the particular Churches, expressing itself in them. ( [+[1]+] ) The approval of a Catechism is the recognition of the fact that it is a text of the universal Church for a given situation and culture.

286. In the formulation of these guidelines and guidelines, no effort has been spared so that all reflection originates and is based on the teachings of the Second Vatican Council and the subsequent and main magisterial interventions of the Church. Likewise, special attention has been paid to the experiences of ecclesial life of the various peoples during this period. In the light of fidelity to the Spirit of God, the necessary discernment has been carried out, always in order to renew the Church and better serve evangelization.

287. The new General Directory for Catechesis is proposed to all the pastors of the Church, their collaborators and catechists, with the hope that it will be an encouragement in the service that the Church and the Spirit entrusts to them: favoring the growth of faith in those who have believed.
288. The effectiveness of catechesis is and will always be a gift from God, through the work of the Spirit of the Father and the Son.

289. Therefore, at the heart of the catechist's spirituality are patience and trust that it is God himself who causes the seed of the Word of God that has been sown in good soil and tilled with love to be born, grow and bear fruit. The evangelist Mark is the only one to collect a parable in which Jesus shows, one after another, the stages of the gradual and constant development of the sown seed: «The Kingdom of God is like a man who casts grain into the ground: whether he sleeps or gets up, night or day, the grain sprouts and grows, without him knowing how. The earth bears the fruit by itself; first grass, then ear, then wheat abundant in the ear. And when the fruit admits it, immediately the sickle is put into it because the harvest has come » ( [+[0]+] ).

290. The Church, which has the responsibility of catechizing those who believe, invokes the Spirit of the Father and the Son, begging Him to make fruitful and interiorly strengthen so many works that are carried out everywhere in favor of the growth of faith and the following of Jesus Christ the Savior.

291. To the Virgin Mary, who saw her Son Jesus "grow in wisdom, age and grace" ([+[0]+]) the catechesis workers also turn today, trusting in her intercession. In Mary they find the spiritual model to promote or consolidate the renewal of contemporary catechesis based on faith, hope and charity. Through the intercession of the "Virgin of Pentecost", ([+[1]+]) may a new strength spring forth in the Church to beget sons and daughters in the faith and educate them towards fullness in Christ.
